description: Sopdet's resplendent rise foretold fertile abundance, as mythical Bennu (Phoenix) stood as an emblem of resilience. Today, a vanguard of young Egyptian women in Computer Science, AI, Data, and Economics carries that sacred legacy into a new epoch. Powered by NASA data, Phoenix Sopdet crafts an AI crop rotation platform with voice guidance. Where heritage and tech converge, we cultivate impact.
summary:
**SOPDET FARMSHIELD – From Stars to Soil**

SOPDET FARMSHIELD is an interactive agricultural decision-support prototype developed by Team PHOENIX SOPDET for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of planning sustainable crop rotations by helping users understand how crop selection, growing seasons, botanical families, and historical climate conditions relate to one another.

Using historical climate data from NASA POWER, FAO-sourced crop reference profiles, and transparent rule-based checks, the platform allows users to explore farm conditions and compare three crop rotation scenarios across four growing seasons. It highlights potential seasonal mismatches and repeated botanical families through interactive dashboards, visualizations, and alerts.

The project is important because it makes complex environmental and agricultural information easier to explore and understand, supporting more informed and climate-aware farming decisions. Inspired by the ancient Egyptian star Sopdet (Sirius), it connects Egypt's agricultural heritage with modern Earth observation technology.

**PHOENIX SOPDET – FROM STARS TO SOIL.**
details:
SOPDET FARMSHIELD — From Stars to Soil

Team: PHOENIX SOPDET
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Project Overview

SOPDET FARMSHIELD is an interactive agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help users explore and compare crop rotation plans across four consecutive growing seasons. It addresses a practical challenge in agriculture: making crop rotation decisions while considering seasonal suitability, botanical family sequences, and historical climate conditions.

Inspired by the ancient Egyptian star Sopdet (Sirius), our project connects Egypt's agricultural heritage with modern Earth observation data. Its guiding idea is simple: From Stars to Soil.

How It Works

The application guides users through a simple workflow:

  1. Farm Setup: Users select a reference location and enter the available farm information.
  2. Dashboard: The application presents historical climate indicators, including temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, and soil moisture-related variables.
  3. Field Insights: Users explore climate information through visual charts and summaries.
  4. Crop Rotation Planner: Users compare three plans: Current Practice, Scenario A, and Scenario B. Each plan covers four growing seasons.
  5. Rule-Based Checks: The planner identifies potential repeated botanical families and seasonal mismatches, displaying understandable alerts to support further review.

Rather than automatically choosing a supposedly perfect plan, SOPDET FARMSHIELD makes differences between scenarios easier to explore and understand.

Data Sources and Methodology

  • NASA POWER: Historical climate data used to provide environmental context for the selected reference locations.
  • FAO-sourced crop reference data: Crop profiles collected, organized, and reviewed by the team.
  • Rule-Based Logic: Transparent checks for crop-family repetition and seasonal alignment.
  • Data Processing: Cleaning, validation, and organization of datasets before integrating them into the application.

We distinguish between documented data and unverified reference inputs. The current prototype does not claim to provide field-level measurements, guaranteed irrigation requirements, or scientifically validated yield predictions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

SOPDET FARMSHIELD aims to:

  • Make agricultural and climate information easier to explore.
  • Help users compare alternative crop rotation sequences.
  • Highlight potential seasonal and botanical-family conflicts.
  • Encourage more informed agricultural planning.
  • Demonstrate how open Earth observation and climate datasets can support practical agricultural tools.

Our long-term vision is to support more informed and climate-aware farming decisions through better integration of local agricultural knowledge and environmental data.

Creativity and Innovation

The project's creative identity combines ancient Egyptian heritage with modern agricultural technology. Sopdet, associated with Sirius in ancient Egyptian tradition, inspired our visual identity and the connection between observing the sky and understanding the land.

Our innovation is also reflected in the way we bring historical climate information, crop reference profiles, and transparent rotation checks together in one interactive experience. Instead of presenting disconnected charts, the application focuses on comparing practical scenarios and explaining potential issues.

Challenges and How We Addressed Them

During development, we faced challenges involving data availability, inconsistent dataset structures, different observation periods, and unclear definitions for some agricultural reference values.

We addressed these challenges by:

  • Prioritizing accessible and traceable NASA POWER datasets.
  • Cleaning and validating the available climate records.
  • Identifying limitations in geographic and temporal coverage.
  • Separating verified climate data from unverified crop reference inputs.
  • Using transparent rule-based checks instead of claiming an untrained AI model or unsupported predictions.

These decisions helped us build a more honest and understandable prototype.

Technologies and Tools

  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • Data Processing: Python and CSV/JSON datasets.
  • Climate Data: NASA POWER.
  • Agricultural References: FAO-sourced crop information.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Node.js, and npm.
  • Visualization: Interactive charts and a location/context interface.

Current Limitations and Future Development

The current prototype uses two reference locations and historical climate records; these locations do not represent entire countries. It uses rule-based logic rather than a trained Machine Learning model.

Future development could include locally verified soil analyses, more geographically detailed datasets, validated crop water requirements, expert-reviewed agricultural rules, and field testing with farmers.

SOPDET FARMSHIELD does not claim to replace agricultural experts. It aims to make available information more accessible, comparisons more transparent, and agricultural planning easier to explore.

PHOENIX SOPDET — FROM STARS TO SOIL.
